_comment: The law each president is best known for, named under the Major laws count on /presidents ('incl. ...'). An editorial pick, not a measure: Mayhew's capitals mark what mattered most to Congress, which favours budget reconciliation acts no reader associates with a president. Each pick must be on that president's Mayhew list, by its title as the site shows it (the law's Congress.gov title from 1973, Mayhew's entry title before); lib/president-data.test.ts checks every pick matches. 'label' is the shorter name readers know it by (NAFTA, not the North American Free Trade Agreement Implementation Act), shown in place of the title. A president with no pick, or a pick that stops matching, falls back to biggestMajorLaw. Checked against a year of English Wikipedia pageviews (Sep 2024-Aug 2025) where the choice was close: NAFTA 568k vs OBRA 1993 22k, ADA 163k vs OBRA 1990 9k, ACA 633k vs the Recovery Act 88k, No Child Left Behind 308k vs EGTRRA 17k.

picks.label: Marshall Plan
picks.why: Rebuilt postwar Western Europe; the defining act of his foreign policy.
Built the Interstate Highway System, which carries his name.

picks.label: Peace Corps Act
picks.why: The program most tied to his call to service.
Ended legal segregation in public places and banned job discrimination.
The core of his environmental record, alongside the EPA he created the same year.

picks.law: Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974
picks.why: Set the rules for private pensions and, later, 401(k) plans.
The tax overhaul that cut rates and closed loopholes.
Banned discrimination against people with disabilities.

picks.law: North American Free Trade Agreement Implementation Act
picks.label: NAFTA

picks.law: No Child Left Behind Act of 2001
picks.why: His signature domestic law: national testing and school accountability.
